messages:
anya: Heads-up — partner integration (PartnerX) is showing ~3k reqs/hr attributed to our internal dev project in billing. partner flagged unexpected charges. noticed spike at 04:11 UTC.

derek: ouch. do we know if they're sending org/project headers or using partner-scoped API keys?

sam: quick look at auth logs: several tokens with prefix `pk_live_partnerx_` have project_id=null but X-Redwood-Project header=partnerx-789. routing still picks project from token_claims when present. sounds like a precedence mismatch.

emily: we intentionally changed precedence last month to prefer token_claims over header to block header spoofing from public clients. but partner proxies might be setting header intentionally for proxy routing.

anya: sample log: ```INFO timestamp=2025-02-12 auth=ok token=pk_live_partnerx_abc header_project=partnerx-789 claims_project= - routed_project=internal-dev routed_pool=dedicated-dev```

derek: so claims empty, header present, but routed_project ended up as internal-dev? how are we mapping that?

sam: finding: when both claims and header empty we fallback to owner_project via api_key -> internal-dev. looks like some tokens aren't parsed early enough and fallback triggers before header middleware runs. race between auth-validators and header-injector middleware.

emily: that's new. middleware ordering regression after the router refactor.

ops-bot: alert: billing-unattributed spike detected: increased unattributed_count by 4200 in 15m window. Paging eng-platform.

anya: immediate options: 1) revert middleware ordering so header runs earlier, 2) revert precedence (header > claims) for partners, 3) change default fallback pool to shared-billing-pool to avoid charging internal project, 4) fail fast and return 4xx for ambiguous attribution.

derek: option 4 will break partners. not acceptable. option 2 is okay short-term but reduces spoof protection. option 3 is safest for customers but pushes cost to us.

sam: finance will care if we take on the bill. but customer trust > short-term cost probably. propose option 3 as immediate mitigation + hotfix ordering change.

emily: +1 to ordering fix as real root cause. I'll patch middleware sequence in canary and add a unit test.

anya: console/product asks for less noisy surface: add a Keys tab banner in partner org if any key had unattributed billing in last 24h. include a link to request refund.

mike: I can add an attribution_heatmap panel to billing dashboard: per-key vs routed_project vs pool. also add metric auth.attribution_conflict=true when header and claims disagree.

sam: let's also emit auth.attribution_source enum ("claims","header","fallback") for every request and a billing.attributed boolean. backfill for last 24h if possible.

canary-bot: deploy started: auth-router v3.1.2 -> canary (10% traffic). change: default_unattributed_pool=shared-billing-pool + telemetry flags enabled.

ops-bot: action: set sampling to 100% for attribution traces for 10m.

canary-bot: canary healthy after 7m. unattributed routing to internal-dev dropped 92%. billing-unattributed delta decreased.

derek: good. next steps: (A) emily reorder middleware + tests (B) anya file finance reconciliation + partner outreach (C) mike telemetry/dashboard PR (D) sam retrospective for precedence decision.

emily: patch uploaded, unit tests added for header-before-claims path. requesting quick review. ```git pr create --title "auth: ensure header injector runs before claims parser" --branch hotfix/middleware-order```

anya: pinged finance + partner success with mitigations and ETA for fix. partner asked for promised credits if affected > $500. I've scheduled a billing review.

sam: long-term item: design signed-header scheme (HMAC) for trusted partner proxies so we can safely accept header precedence without spoof risk. add to roadmap.

mike: noted dashboard followups and alert thresholds. will post a dashboard link in followup issue.

anya: thanks team. leaning to keep default_shared pool for unattributed for 48h while middleware fix rolls out. will escalate if finance objects. :wave:

ops-bot: incident status: mitigated (default pool set to shared-billing-pool + middleware reorder in canary). monitoring 24h.
